findings.evidence: When spill is triggered after result generation has started, `pkg/executor/sortexec/sort.go:452-479` calls `spillSortedRowsInMemory()` → `spillHelper.spillImpl(e.Parallel.merger)` and only clears `e.Parallel.sortedRowsIters` in the deferred cleanup (`pkg/executor/sortexec/sort.go:440-443`). But `spillImpl()` unconditionally calls `releaseMemory()` (`pkg/executor/sortexec/parallel_sort_spill_helper.go:155-162`) which subtracts `worker.totalMemoryUsage` from `sortExec.memTracker` without clearing those in-memory row references. Second confirmation: `chunk.Row` retains a `*chunk.Chunk` (`pkg/util/chunk/row.go:29-32`) and `Iterator4Slice` holds `[]Row` (`pkg/util/chunk/iterator.go:65-69`), so the original input chunks remain reachable until the deferred `Reset(nil)` runs, even though the tracker is already decremented.
findings.fix: After a successful in-memory spill (the `spillSortedRowsInMemory()` path), immediately drop in-memory references before/with the accounting update: e.g. reset all `e.Parallel.sortedRowsIters[i].Reset(nil)` (and any other holders like worker-local iterators/merger) right after spilling, then apply `releaseMemory()`; or make `spillImpl` accept a callback to clear references prior to `releaseMemory()`.
findings.impact: Memory-quota behavior can be incorrect: the sort executor can report freed memory while still retaining large input chunks, undermining OOM/spill decisions for the rest of the statement and increasing risk of process-level OOM or severe memory pressure (especially with large sorts and slow consumers where spill is triggered mid-output).
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943): the same pattern remains (spill via `spillSortedRowsInMemory()` with iterator clearing only in the `generateResult` defer; `releaseMemory()` still only adjusts the tracker).
findings.verify: Add/extend a unit test that triggers spill mid-output (like the existing manual-trigger path) and asserts that after spill the executor drops `sortedRowsIters` references (or at least that tracked memory does not drop unless references are cleared). Scenario-wise: run a large sort with a low mem quota and an intentionally slow result consumer; verify RSS/heap does not remain dominated by the original in-memory chunks after spill is triggered.
findings.what: Parallel sort spill triggered during result generation adjusts memory tracking as if input chunks were released, but keeps `sortedRowsIters` (and thus `chunk.Row` → `*Chunk`) alive until executor teardown, defeating spill’s purpose and potentially bypassing memory-quota enforcement.

subject: executor: Support parallel sort spill (#50747)
summary: Commit adds parallel sort spill support with a shared multi-way merge and spill helper. Main correctness risk: on the “in-memory then spill” path, it decrements memory tracking without promptly dropping in-memory row/chunk references, so actual memory pressure may not be relieved and quota enforcement can be bypassed.
